---
title: "A7 high-temperature pressure comparison"
---

A7 comparison record; adopted parameter identity linked from the [overview](../notebook.qmd#working-record).

# Question

How well does A7 reproduce the retained high-temperature CO₂ pressures?

# Result

A7 predicts the 54 canonical 100–120 °C pressures with 24.3% AARD, ranging from 18.5% (Mamun 2005, 120 °C) to 31.5% (Jou 1995, 120 °C). These are non-fitted predictions and do not qualify high-temperature process use.

# Basis and method

Average absolute relative deviation (AARD) is computed within each named retained cohort; source, temperature, pressure basis and row availability remain in the source-state assessment.

# Values

## Cohort comparison {#high-temperature-pressure-comparison}

A7’s 100–120 °C comparisons preserve source and cohort membership from [state-targets.csv](../results/engine-3e83e19c-paper-evidence/state-targets.csv). The packet view contains the same Jou rows as the canonical view; the two Jou source/temperature rows below each represent both views.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical, 100–120 °C | 54 | 24.35 |
| Packet (Jou subset), 100–120 °C | 20 | 27.51 |
| Jou 1995, 100 °C (canonical and packet) | 10 | 23.49 |
| Jou 1995, 120 °C (canonical and packet) | 10 | 31.52 |
| Mamun 2005, 120 °C | 19 | 18.57 |
| Xu 2011, 100 °C | 8 | 26.90 |
| Xu 2011, 120 °C | 7 | 28.09 |

<!-- RESULTS:high-temperature:END -->

# Limits and evidence type

These are non-fitted comparisons at the retained source states. Data-access history and overlapping membership limit an independent-prediction interpretation. No matched no-heat calculation was made.
